title: Choi Bul-am used stage name; Choi Young-han remembered as Korea's national father
text:
Choi Bul-am used stage name; Choi Young-han remembered as Korea's national father - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 2일(월) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Entertainment Choi Bul-am used stage name; Choi Young-han remembered as Korea's national father 
 입력 2026.11.02. 00:00 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 A national actor, the late Choi Bul-am, left behind a substantial legacy. Among this, a special family story related to the stage name, which had been previously reported, also draws attention. 
 On the 1st, KBS1 aired the second part of the special documentary "Table keeper Choi Bul-am, we will remember you," which looked back on the late man's life and acting career and mourned the "national father" who left a significant mark on Korea's broadcasting history.
 Choi Bul-am began his acting career on the theater stage in 1959 and from the 1960s was active in broadcasting, establishing himself as a national actor. In particular, on MBC's "Investigation chief" he played the righteous Chief Park, and in the national drama "Rural Diary" he played the benevolent Chairman Kim, sharing joys and sorrows with viewers for many years. With his distinctive deep voice and warm acting, he even earned the moniker "national father."
 Tributes from fellow actors who had worked with him continued. Actor Lee Gye-in recalled that Choi Bul-am was a person who approached acting throughout his life with exceptional pride and responsibility in the profession. Chae Sira said, "It was an honor to work together on three projects: twice as father roles and once as a grandfather role," recalling her special connection with the late man. She especially noted that she learned from his obsession with acting and his approach of digging deeply. Recalling how in the drama "Widow" he even expressed the scene of meeting death with delicate differences, she said, "He truly was a teacher. Simply watching him was a lesson," expressing her respect.
 The tribute from Kim Hye-ja, who had played a married couple with him for many years on "Rural Diary," brought even more poignancy. Kim Hye-ja said, "It doesn't feel like this is the last. When you die, we'll meet again," and added, "Don't say it's the last." She conveyed that she would live remembering the numerous memories with the late man for the rest of her life. Cha In-pyo also said, "Through the living-room stage, he long played the role of father to the entire nation," expressing gratitude to the late man who gave courage and consolation to the people from difficult times up to recently. Choi Soo-jong remembered Choi Bul-am as an elder who provided great comfort and strength that supported his life. He vowed not to forget the late man's habit of always looking out for those in low places and the positive influence he spread.
 In fact, the unique name Choi Bul-am was known to be a stage name. His real name was Choi Young-han. The late man's father ran a newspaper company and a film company during his lifetime but collapsed from overwork and died at the young age of 35. Worried that Choi Bul-am might follow the same path as his father, the elder uncle took a name from Bulam Mountain and gave him the new name "Bul-am."
 The name "Choi Bul-am," born in this way, later remained as the name of a national actor representing Korea, and the late man's real name "Choi Young-han" also drew attention on his final path. At the funeral hall, a black-and-white portrait of the late man smiling brightly was hung outside the wake, and on the nameplate his real name "Choi Young-han" was written instead of the stage name "Choi Bul-am," which the public knew. The sight of the late man, who had stood by the public his whole life as "Choi Bul-am," returning to his real name on his final path made the moment even more poignant.
 The name "Choi Bul-am" began from the family's concern for a father who died at 35. Having walked the path of an actor under that new name, he lived for many years as the nation's father, leaving comfort and inspiration to countless people.
 Meanwhile, Choi Bul-am died on Oct. 29 at the age of 87.
